doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: Learning from his father and early country club work
summary: His father taught him what a keyboard player wants; at about 14 he did country club work and took a show he could not read.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Gosh. Did you have to read a bigger book to get a bass drum? Well that’s great. So your first real playing experience was with your father. Then you started branching out and playing with local people?

Yes. Well he was a task master, and he taught me well. To be taught from another musician is quite interesting. To be taught from another drummer is one aspect and certainly a requirement. But to have a keyboard player tell you what a keyboard wants to hear out of you, definitely added something to my playing. And I use that. To this day I’ll ask other instruments what they like to hear out of me at different times during a tune. So to answer your question, my father was a well known area musician, and sooner or later other bands got stuck for a drummer, and I was asked. And I was playing out quite a bit because I was able to — I knew a lot of the commercial tunes and I did a lot of the country club work.
And the country club work requires a specific kind of thing, like how old were you when you started doing that?
So if the leader of the band called a tune and said to you, “Businessman’s bounce,” you knew what that meant?
Exactly. Because I was exposed to it in my household before I was born.
That must have been pretty neat for the musicians — hey, wow, the kid knows what it is.

Yeah it was. It was, of course it got me into trouble eventually because my father was a well known musician, and I got pushed along too fast. I knew these things, and eventually someone called up for a show, and I took it. And I thought I could cut it because I could read some of the exercises, and I couldn’t. And it tainted me for a while. The next day I made an appointment with a drum teacher who could read and was experienced in shows, and within two years I could play a show fluently.
